name: Citizenship by Marriage (Foreign Wife of a Jordanian Man)

qualifying_event.description: A foreign woman married to a Jordanian man may acquire Jordanian nationality by written declaration after Council of Ministers approval, once the marriage has lasted the qualifying period (Nationality Law No. 6 of 1954, as amended). There is no equivalent provision in the law for a foreign man married to a Jordanian woman.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Marriage certificate; declaration submitted after the qualifying marriage duration.

requirement_groups.name: Arab wife of a Jordanian man

requirements.blocker_text: 3 years of marriage to a Jordanian man, for a wife of Arab nationality.

requirement_groups.name: Non-Arab wife of a Jordanian man

requirements.blocker_text: 5 years of marriage to a Jordanian man, for a wife of non-Arab nationality.

evidence_required.document: Written declaration of intent to acquire nationality

sources.title: Refworld (UNHCR) -- Jordan Nationality Law No. 6 of 1954, as amended to 1987: after Council of Ministers approval, a foreign wife of a Jordanian man may acquire nationality by written declaration -- 3 years of marriage for an Arab wife, 5 years for a non-Arab wife; no comparable provision exists for a foreign husband of a Jordanian woman

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Jordan). STATUS: DRAFT -- tier-2 sourced (Refworld hosting of the law text, not Jordan's own gazette). IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL FINDING: this route is explicitly and asymmetrically gendered. Jordan's Nationality Law grants a path to citizenship for a foreign WIFE of a Jordanian man (3yr Arab / 5yr non-Arab, subject to Council approval) but contains NO equivalent provision for a foreign HUSBAND of a Jordanian woman -- a Jordanian woman cannot pass citizenship to her foreign spouse through marriage at all under this law. This is a well-documented feature of Jordanian nationality law (and shared by several other countries in the region) and is modeled here as a genuine, disclosed asymmetry rather than smoothed into a gender-neutral 'spouse' framing -- consistent with this dataset's convention of disclosing structural absences rather than inventing symmetry that doesn't exist. A Jordanian woman's foreign husband and their children face separate, well-documented statelessness/residency complications (their children do not receive citizenship automatically either -- see jo_citizenship_by_descent.json) that are not modeled as a route here since no legal citizenship pathway exists for them to model.
